questions.question: What must drivers do when entering a roundabout or traffic circle?

options.text: Always stop before entering.
Yield to drivers already in the roundabout or traffic circle.
Have the right-of-way if there is one lane.
Have the right-of-way if there are two lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already in the roundabout or traffic circle.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout or traffic circle, you must let drivers already inside go first.

questions.question: How should you look for a gap in traffic when entering a freeway on the entrance ramp?

options.text: Look in the inside rearview mirror only.
Look in the side view mirror only.
Look in both the rearview and side view mirrors.
Look in your mirrors and turn your head to look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look in your mirrors and turn your head to look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Check both your mirrors and look over your shoulder to find a safe gap in traffic on the freeway.

questions.question: What does a flashing red light at a railroad crossing mean?

options.text: Stop. Do not go until the signals stop flashing.
Slow down and go if the tracks are clear.
Go slowly and carefully.
You have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop. Do not go until the signals stop flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad crossings when you see flashing red lights, a lowered gate, a person signaling, or hear a train whistle. Never go around a gate or ignore these warning signs.

questions.question: How many hours of sleep should teenagers get each night to avoid drowsy driving crashes?

options.text: Seven hours
Six hours
Eight hours
Nine hours

questions.explanation: Teenagers who sleep less than eight hours a night are more likely to have car crashes.

questions.question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?

options.text: When pulling toward or away from a curb.
When turning left or right.
When changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you move your vehicle. This includes turning, changing lanes, and pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: What should you do before starting your car?

options.text: Check that only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Check that only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Check that only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Check that all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Before starting the car, make sure you and all passengers buckle your seat belts.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes on a highway?

options.text: Signal your lane change.
Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When changing lanes, signal first, check both mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Keep your tires filled with the right air pressure.
Replace tires with worn tread.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your car slides on water between the tires and road. You can reduce this risk by slowing down on wet roads, keeping tires properly filled, and replacing worn tires.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow traffic light?

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep going because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Watch what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on wet roads?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit.
Drive faster than the speed limit.
Slow down by five to ten miles per hour.
Stay close to the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down by five to ten miles per hour.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, reduce your speed by five to ten miles per hour to stay safe.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement gradually.
Slam on your brakes and stop.
Slow down gently with the brakes. Then turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gently with the brakes. Then turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your wheels leave the road, keep driving on the shoulder and gently apply the brakes to slow down. Once you reach a safe speed, turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement. Do not jerk the steering wheel sharply.

questions.question: You missed your exit on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Go to the next exit.
Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for an escort back to your exit.

questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, continue to the next exit. Do not stop, back up, or cross the median on the highway. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver who arrives first.
The driver who arrives last.
One driver should continue without stopping.
One driver should wave others ahead.

questions.explanation: All four drivers must stop at a four-way stop. The first driver to arrive goes through first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the one on the right goes first.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A divided highway ends.
A one-way street begins.
A one-way street ends.
A divided highway begins.

questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road ahead is a divided highway. Stay to the right of the divider or median.

questions.question: You arrive at an intersection with no signs or signals at the same time as a vehicle on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and go through the intersection.
Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
Drive through and make the other vehicle stop.
Honk and drive through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Let that vehicle pass before you proceed.

questions.question: What do your brake lights tell other drivers?

options.text: You are making a turn.
Your emergency brake is on.
You are changing lanes.
You are slowing down or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are slowing down or stopping.
questions.explanation: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping. Keep your brake lights in working order at all times.

questions.question: When is it okay NOT to stop for a school bus with red lights flashing and its stop arm extended?

options.text: You are driving on the opposite side of a divided highway.
You are behind the bus.
You see no children present.
You can safely pass on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are driving on the opposite side of a divided highway.
questions.explanation: The only time you do not have to stop for a school bus with flashing lights and its stop arm extended is if you are on the opposite side of a divided highway.

questions.question: When approaching a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended, what should you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn and pass on the left.
Keep driving once you think most children are done exiting.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when approaching a stopped school bus with its stop signal on. Do not move until the stop arm is withdrawn.
